habitat: Well-grassed bushveld, vleis, streams, rank grass in old cultivations, and hillsides. In summer the male flies with a spread tail or perches on bushes.
summary: A common, localised resident. The breeding male has only a narrow red collar, often hard to see, and a long thin tail, much smaller than Long-tailed Widowbird. The display call is a weak kizz-zizz-zizz-zizz and a blowing sound. The female and non-breeding male were not described. The Kemp paper name Redcollared Widow and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: White-winged Widowbird has a yellow-and-white shoulder and a broad tail, not a narrow red collar.

head.pattern: Narrow red collar, often difficult to see. Newman does not name the body colour.

tail.shape: Long and thin, spread in display.

viewNotes.note: Breeding male: narrow red collar and a long thin tail.
The red collar can be difficult to see from the front.
Long thin tail. Newman does not name the back colour.
A flight pattern was not described.

calls.description: When displaying, a weak kizz-zizz-zizz-zizz and a blowing sound. Grade A call and song from Rietvlei Nature Reserve, with other species in the background. The filename is XC364550-Widowbird Redcollared_RV_161230_10_B_edit.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common, localised resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The female and non-breeding male were not described. The Kruger breeding male is distant. A streaked frame was not used because that plumage was not described. No flight photograph was found. Population figures and the Kemp name Redcollared Widow were left unchanged.
